definition: Provisions establishing a broad mutual waiver of claims among all signatory parties to a multiparty IPD agreement, subject only to narrowly enumerated exceptions (e.g., willful misconduct, statutory violations, warranty failures, non-payment, IP infringement, insured claims, third-party claims, undiscoverable substantial defects), together with a waiver of consequential/indirect damages and indemnification obligations limited to available insurance proceeds (other than for bodily injury/property damage claims).
include_when: Apply when a clause establishes a general inter-party waiver of claims among the signatories to a multiparty/IPD agreement (as opposed to a two-party indemnity or disclaimer), enumerates exceptions to that waiver, waives consequential/indirect damages among the parties, or ties indemnification obligations to available insurance proceeds as the primary or sole measure of liability.
exclude_when: Do not apply to bilateral risk-allocation/disclaimer clauses between an Owner and a single Contractor/Design-Builder (see C11); do not apply to clauses solely defining privity boundaries with non-signatory third parties absent a mutual waiver structure (see C20); do not apply to insurance coverage-scope clauses that do not also establish a liability-limitation/waiver function (see C32, C39).
memo: New code capturing CCDC 30's Part 10 (Liability Allocation), specifically GC 10.1.1's broad mutual waiver of claims among the Owner, Consultant, Contractor and Other IPD Parties subject to eight enumerated exceptions, GC 10.1.2's mutual waiver of consequential/indirect/special/punitive damages, and GC 10.2.1-10.2.4's indemnification obligations generally limited to available insurance proceeds (except for third-party bodily injury/property damage claims, which remain unlimited). This 'no-blame culture' liability-sharing architecture is central to the IPD/alliance literature (T9) on relational contracting as an enabler of collaborative MMC/prefabrication coordination -- it removes the adversarial fault-finding incentive that the literature associates with fragmented risk allocation in traditional delivery models, and is identifiable at clause/sub-clause level (GC 10.1.1-10.1.3, GC 10.2.1-10.2.6). It is absent from every bilateral CCDC form reviewed (CCDC 2/2 CcQ/3/5A/5B/14/17), all of which instead employ unilateral risk-transfer/disclaimer language (see C11) or two-party indemnification. This code is analytically distinct from C11 (unilateral risk transfer typically to the contractor), C20 (privity boundaries with non-signatory third parties), and C39 (design-specific insurance/cap), making it useful for comparing how IPD-style multiparty agreements versus bilateral CCDC forms structure inter-party liability in ways directly relevant to collaborative MMC/prefabrication delivery.

label: Dynamic Work Scope Reallocation and Profit-Pool Rebalancing Clause
definition: Provisions permitting a joint governance body (e.g., a Project Management Team) to increase or decrease the work scope assigned to a member of a multiparty delivery team after Contract execution, including rules for self-performed trade work bid competitively against subcontractors, and consequential rebalancing of shared profit/incentive pools.
include_when: Apply when a clause permits mid-project reassignment or reallocation of scope of Design Services or Work among signatory parties or members of a delivery team (as opposed to third-party subcontractors), or establishes a mechanism for a Contractor/Construction Manager to compete to self-perform trade work otherwise intended for subcontractors, together with any consequential adjustment to a shared incentive/profit pool.
exclude_when: Do not apply to ordinary Subcontractor/Supplier nomination, objection or substitution clauses governing third-party engagement (see C33); do not apply to general scope-of-work/roles definition clauses absent a reallocation mechanism (see C35); do not apply to ordinary change-order valuation of scope changes instructed by an Owner to a single Contractor (see C7).
memo: New code capturing CCDC 30's GC 4.1 (Reallocation of Work Scope) and GC 4.2 (Self-Performed Trade Work). GC 4.1.1-4.1.2 allow the PMT to increase or reduce any Design/Construction Team member's work scope to reduce the Estimated Final Cost, improve schedule/quality, or otherwise benefit the Project, with the PMT empowered to recalculate Profit Pool distributions where reallocation creates material financial inequity, recorded via Contract Amendment. GC 4.2.1-4.2.3 permit the Contractor to submit competing proposals to self-perform trade work, with differentiated overhead/profit treatment depending on whether the work is awarded on a competitive lump-sum basis (no additional overhead or Profit Pool adjustment) or a negotiated reimbursable-cost basis (profit added to and Profit Pool distributions proportionately adjusted). This mid-project scope-reallocation and self-performance mechanism is directly relevant to MMC/prefabrication literature on flexible allocation of manufacturing/fabrication responsibility among project participants (e.g., shifting installation work toward or away from off-site trade packages after signing), is identifiable at clause/sub-clause level, is unique to CCDC 30 among the forms reviewed (absent from all bilateral CCDC forms), and is analytically distinct from the general scope-definition code (C35) and the third-party qualification/selection code (C33), justifying a dedicated new code.
